messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@healthscope.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick ask: per-1M token input/output rates + model list for hosted API

Hi Naomi,

We kicked off a short pilot evaluation at HealthScope and I need to get a baseline unit economics number to model cost. Can you share Redwood's standard hosted API IO rates (per 1M tokens) split by input vs output, and any notes on how streaming tokens are billed? Also — what models are currently supported for hosted (and which are certified for production)?

A couple quick context points so you can tailor the reply:
- Pilot expected traffic (avg): ~500k input tokens/day, ~2M output tokens/day during inference bursts
- Latency target: 300–500ms P90 for chat-style generation
- We're interested in model options that support streaming and quantized variants for cost control

If you can paste the per-1M numbers and attach a simple model-compat roster I can hand to our finance lead, that would be ideal. If it helps, happy to schedule a 20-minute sync.

Thanks —
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform
HealthScope AI
liam@healthscope.ai

Hi Liam —

Thanks for the context — appreciate the traffic sample. High-level answers below so you can get started; I attached a short preview rate card and a CSV of currently supported serving models for hosted (production vs beta): healthscope_rate_preview_v1.pdf; pilot_supported_models.csv.

Baseline hosted IO (standard, retail rates, per 1M tokens) — region US:
- Input (tokens consumed in prompt / user input): $0.80 per 1M tokens
- Output (tokens generated by model): $1.20 per 1M tokens

Notes:
- Streaming responses are billed on the generated tokens as they stream (output side). Input tokens are billed at the time of request. There is no separate streaming surcharge.
- Embeddings and special reranker endpoints are billed separately — I can include those if relevant.
- We publish discounted tiers for committed volumes (monthly/annual) — typical pilot customers remain on retail while we size production.

Model availability (attached CSV includes family, quantized variants, and a production-certified flag). Short summary:
- Redwood-Base and Redwood-2 families (production-certified) — good latency/cost balance and recommended for streaming.
- A curated set of LLMs from the open model catalog (some listed as beta for hosted).

Quick follow-up Qs to make the numbers more precise:
1) Will you want a committed monthly token tier if production looks viable? (Discounting differs by commit length.)
2) Are you planning to use embedding or reranking endpoints during the pilot (affects separate IO lines)?
3) Any regulatory residency or private deployment needs (VPC/on-prem) for this pilot?

If you want, I can put Ben (Sales Ops) on the thread and ask him to paste the formal retail/volume-breakdown table so you have a clean set of numbers for finance. Otherwise we can lock a 20-minute call — I'm available Fri morning PST.

Best,

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@healthscope.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API — retail rates + volume bands (canonical)

Hi Liam — looping in the canonical numbers below. Naomi & I discussed and I'm sending the retail table and typical discount bands (these are standard for hosted API pilots; custom enterprise terms require an SOW). Attachments: healthscope_rate_preview_v1.pdf (preview) and pilot_supported_models.csv (model roster).

Retail per 1M tokens (US region):
- Input: $0.80 / 1M tokens
- Output: $1.20 / 1M tokens

Volume bands (monthly committed tokens, applies to total billed tokens (input+output)):
- 0 — 5M: retail (0% off)
- >5M — 50M: 10% off retail
- >50M — 250M: 20% off retail
- >250M: custom enterprise pricing (contact Sales)

Notes on billing and caching:
- Billing is token-based at request time. Prefix/KV caching reduces compute and latency but cached tokens are not automatically credited; however effective per-token cost is lower due to reduced model work. For committed discounts we apply the discount to billed tokens (no retroactive credits for cached tokens).
- Streaming: billed as output tokens as they are generated.
- Quantized model variants: same IO billing; quantization affects instance cost (reflected in our model choices) not token billing.

Example calculation (retail):
- Session: 400k input + 1.6M output = 2.0M tokens/day
- Retail daily cost = (0.80 * 0.4) + (1.20 * 1.6) per 1M scaled = $0.32 + $1.92 = $2.24 per day (note: using per-1M rates scaled to millions)
- Monthly (30-day) retail = $67.20

At 20% discount (applies when total monthly tokens >50M):
- Discounted input rate = $0.64 / 1M; discounted output rate = $0.96 / 1M
- Discounted daily cost = (0.64 * 0.4) + (0.96 * 1.6) = $0.256 + $1.536 = $1.792 per day
- Monthly (30-day) discounted = $53.76

Supported models (summary — see attached CSV for full row-level data):
- Redwood-Base-v1 (production-certified) — streaming, low-latency, recommended default
- Redwood-2-small/medium (production-certified) — better throughput/cost tradeoffs
- OptQuant family (beta) — quantized flavors available, recommended for cost experiments
- A curated set of OSS LLMs (some hosted in beta)

If you want a one-page PDF for finance with the bands and the example calc, I can produce that quickly. Naomi — we can propose Fri 09:00 PST for a 20-minute alignment; I'll be on if that's helpful.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
